REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JANUARY 12, 2023 - 07:00 P.M.
CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL CHAMBER
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703
* COVID-19 NOTICE *
To protect public health and safety during the COVID-19 pandemic and in compliance with the current State Department of Public Health and Los Angeles County Health Officer Orders and City of Cerritos COVID-19 Safety Plan, the City Council Chamber will be open to the public. As authorized by State of California Executive Orders N-25-20, N-29-20, and N-08-21, and subsequently by Assembly Bill 361 (Chapter 165, Statutes of 2021) and City Council Resolution No. 2022-10 adopted pursuant thereto, this meeting may also be conducted via teleconference, if necessary. Public observation and participation in this meeting will be facilitated through the methods described below.
Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in-person in the Council Chamber subject to posted COVID-19 protocols.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in-person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Rory Corrigan, Church in Cerritos.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Whitney High School Mock Trial Team.

5.  Presentations/Appointments

  Korean American Day (accepted by Mid-City Korean American Seniors Association). A Korean
  American Day proclamation was also presented from Assemblymember Sharon Quirk-Silva
  by Joe Pak, Field Representative.

  Whitney High School Mock Trial Team (3rd Place, Senior Division, Los Angeles County Mock
  Trial Program).

  PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  There was no action taken on this item.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  The Mayor opened the public comments period.

  In-Person Public Comments:

  David Pylman expressed concerns regarding the audio-visual presentations displayed
  during the January 11, 2023 Planning Commission meeting and requested access to the
  City’s audio and visual systems for use by the public during City public meetings.

  Sarah Ornelas and Bonnie Ornelas requested the City Council consider expansion of the
  City Dial-a-Ride program’s service area.

  CONSENSUS (Vo): Directed the City Manager to provide a report to the City Council on
  the feasibility of expanding the Cerritos Dial-a-Ride program service area.

  Joan Pylman expressed concern with the delay of completion of the Del Amo Boulevard
  Bridge Replacement and Signal Enhancements Project, requested removal of the
  billboard adjacent to the project area, and inquired whether a regular project status
  update to residents living in the adjacent area could be provided. The speaker submitted
  a document for the record entitled, “Agenda Report (Item 9E, June 8, 2020).”
  (Documents submitted during public comments are considered public records and are
  available by request at the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer).

  Alfred Reyes requested a more contemporary line-up for scheduled performances at the
  Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts and expressed concern regarding the
  involvement of the outgoing City Manager in performance selections for the upcoming
  season.

  Case van der Linden expressed concern with the condition of streets throughout the
  community.

  Written Correspondence:
  (Written correspondence is considered public record. Full-text copies of submitted
  written correspondence can be obtained in the Office of the City Clerk/Treasurer)

  Malik Tariq Mahmood shared a personal message of faith from the 10th Annual Peace
  Symposium.

  Steven Hsieh requested timely repair of potholes throughout the City.

  Brian Hews expressed concern regarding the lack of community engagement as related
  to the subject matter under consideration in agenda item 7E.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  Staff reports were given by Sandy Cisneros, Current Planning Manager, and the City’s

  In-Person Public Comments:

  Joseph Gonzalez, representing Supporters Alliance for Environmental Responsibility
  (“SAFER”), expressed various concerns regarding the environmental impacts of the
  project. He referred to a letter submitted as written correspondence for the record by
  SAFER (document is detailed in the “Written Correspondence” section below).

  Danny McKenna spoke in in support of the proposed project and expressed concerns
  regarding the comments given by the previous public speaker. He confirmed he would

  requesting adequate California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) review of the project.

  Noting there were no other individuals who elected to provide public comment, the
  Mayor declared the public comments period and public hearing closed.

  official record contains all required information related to CEQA studies for the subject

  include in its findings to ensure the record reflects compliance with Cerritos Municipal

  included in any official resolutions adopted to approve the subject project.

  Furthermore, the Cerritos City Council further finds that the City is in compliance
  with Chapter 22.80 of the Cerritos Municipal Code. Chapter 22.80 of the Cerritos
  Municipal Code, as referenced in this resolution, primarily is intended to ensure
  specified environmental performance standards are met when there is an actual
  and ongoing authorized use on any property within the City of Cerritos.
  Additionally, Section 22.80.240 of the Cerritos Municipal Code grants discretion
  to the director of Community Development to determine whether there is cause
  to believe that a proposed use may be in violation of the environmental
  performance standards, and grants discretion to initiate an investigation to
  determine compliance with such standards. For the proposed project, it is
  determined that there is no cause to believe there would be a violation of

  the categorical exemption, including the evidence provided by the consultants to
  address and review traffic, noise, air quality and greenhouse gas emissions; and
